newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington blames profit drop on Europe.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington blames profit drop on Europe.

text.p: British glassmaker Pilkington Plc on Thursday blamed a sharp drop in 1996/1997 pre-tax profits on weak European markets, which it said masked improvements in its business elsewhere.
Pre-tax profits before exceptional items slumped to 132 million pounds ($215.4 million) from 212 million the previous financial year.
The company said it was too early to make a forecast for the 1997/98 financial year, but warned that trading conditions in its core European markets remained tough.

"Conditions in Europe remain difficult and prices fragile. North American economic activity is running at a high level and we continue to grow our businesses in the emerging markets of the world," the company said in a statement.
Paolo Scaroni recently took over as chief executive and chairman Nigel Rudd signalled he had high hopes the new man would be able to make a difference.

"I am confident that under his leadership we can accelerate the pace of change, particularly in Europe, so that the Group can generate more satisfactory cash and profit returns," he said in the statement.
